Let $H$ be the number of hexagonal faces. Count incidences of a vertex with a hexagonal face. Each hexagon has six vertices, so there are $6H$ incidences. Each of the $60$ vertices belongs to exactly two hexagons, so there are also $120$ incidences. Thus
\[
6H=120,\qquad\boxed{H=20}.
\]
Likewise, pentagon-vertex incidences give $5P=60$, so $P=12$ and $H+P=32$, as required.

If counting all face-vertex incidences at once, the correct equation is $6H+5P=3\cdot60$. The factor of two for hexagons belongs on the vertex-counting side of the first equation; inserting it again into $6H$ counts those incidences twice.\begin{asy}
